items.followUp: Define gravitational field strength at a point and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Gravitational field strength is defined as gravitational force per unit mass.
rubric.description: States the defining relationship for gravitational field strength.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as gravitational force per unit mass, or giving F/m.

rubric.why: Dividing force by mass gives the SI unit newton per kilogram.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of gravitational field strength.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for N/kg or newtons per kilogram.

modelAnswer: Gravitational field strength at a point is the gravitational force acting per unit mass placed at that point.
Its SI unit is newton per kilogram (N/kg).

items.followUp: Estimate the age of a 15-year-old in seconds. Take one year as 365 days.

rubric.why: The conversion uses 365 days per year, 24 hours per day, 60 minutes per hour and 60 seconds per minute.
rubric.description: Sets up the conversion from years to seconds correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct multiplication or an equivalent conversion.

rubric.why: This is the estimated age in seconds using 365 days per year.
rubric.description: Gives the estimated age with the correct unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for approximately 630,720,000 seconds, or 6.31 × 10⁸ seconds.

modelAnswer: Given: age = 20 years; 1 year = 365 days; 1 day = 24 hours; 1 hour = 60 minutes; 1 minute = 60 seconds.
Formula: time in seconds = number of years × 365 × 24 × 60 × 60.
